findings.issue_text: `packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119` — null deref. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Now any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar (empty array — which several migrated call sites now produce instead of `null`) throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`, killing the booking. Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-154` — unrelated change that inverts logic. Was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`; now both are gated on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? ... : {}`. With billing enabled the org now gets a real `slug` immediately (bypassing the pending-slug flow); with billing disabled it gets neither slug nor requestedSlug. Revert this hunk — it is out of scope for the PR and is a behavior regression.

`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256` and `:315-317` — self-referential lookup. `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and always returns `undefined`. The previous fallback to the destination calendar's `externalId` is silently gone, so updates/deletes for references without a stored `externalCalendarId` (all pre-existing bookings) now hit `primary`/undefined instead of the destination calendar. Fix: fall back to the first destination calendar (or match by `credentialId`, as `createEvent` does).

`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1080` — the collective calendars are dropped when there is no primary. `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops. A collective event where only non-organizer hosts have destination calendars writes to none of them — the exact case the PR targets. Build the array first, then assign.

`packages/core/EventManager.ts:352-372` and `:504-524`; `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:428-440` — the same "credential not in `this.calendarCredentials`, fetch from DB" block is copy-pasted three times, inside `for` loops (N+1 queries per host), and in `updateAllCalendarEvents` the DB lookup can still leave `credential` `undefined`, which is then passed straight to `updateEvent(credential, ...)` (typed `CredentialWithAppName`, not optional). Extract one helper, batch with `findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`, and guard the undefined case.

`packages/core/EventManager.ts:377-383` — in the fallback branch (destination without `credentialId`, i.e. legacy rows) `createEvent(c, event)` is called with no `externalId`, so the resulting reference gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` where previously it was `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Combined with issue 3, subsequent updates/deletes for those bookings lose their calendar target. Pass `destination.externalId`.

Only `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` was taught about multiple destinations. Office365, Lark, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (CalDAV) all take `destinationCalendar[0]`, so a collective event with Outlook/CalDAV hosts writes every host's event into the main host's calendar (or, for Lark, throws "no calendar id"). At minimum this asymmetry needs a comment/issue; ideally the `credentialId` param added to the `Calendar.createEvent` signature is honored there too.

`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:466-478` — the legacy (no `credentialId`) branch now sits inside the per-reference loop, so with N references it issues N × M delete calls across all calendar credentials, many with mismatched uids. Hoist the legacy path outside the loop, or dedupe.

No tests. This changes a core type used across the booking lifecycle and adds new multi-host branching; the only test touched is a Playwright fixture (`destinationCalendar: null` → `[]`). At least a unit test for `createAllCalendarEvents` with two destinations, and one for the empty-array Meet path (issue 1), are warranted.

`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724-760` — `loadUsers` was rewritten well beyond the PR scope: the dynamic-user query dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` even though `IsFixedAwareUser` declares `organization: { slug: string }` (masked by the `as IsFixedAwareUser[]` cast at line 870), and the new try/catch converts any Prisma error into a generic 500 while swallowing the original. Restore the `organization` select and narrow the catch, or drop the rewrite.

`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:686-688` — `SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE` enum comparisons replaced with string literals `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)`, and the new code elsewhere compares `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. Losing the enum loses compile-time safety if the enum changes. Keep `SchedulingType`.

`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1000-1003` — `firstName: ""`, `lastName: ""` added to team members with no explanation; unrelated to the PR and may overwrite name rendering downstream.
`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182` — `schedulingType` added to `CalendarEvent` and set in `handleNewBooking`, but never read anywhere in this diff. Either use it or drop it.

Repeated `x ? [x] : y ? [y] : []` ternary at ~8 call sites; a tiny `toDestinationCalendarArray(a, b)` helper would keep this consistent (note `bookingReminder.ts` and `webhook.ts` use `[]` while `handleNewBooking` uses `null` for the same "none" case).

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

The proposed fix (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) would prevent the null/undefined deref.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback logic was changed to:

`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the branch where the `find` runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will typically return no match and therefore `undefined`. This removes the previous behavior that fell back to the destination calendar’s externalId (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it wasn’t an array), meaning updates/deletes without a stored `externalCalendarId` will likely target `primary`/default or fail instead of the intended destination calendar. The issue is directly verifiable from the diff and matches the finding’s description.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` and `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` still derive `calendarId` from only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and ignore which credential/destination is currently being processed. This means when creating events for multiple destinations/credentials, these services can use the main host’s destination calendar externalId (or throw if the first entry doesn’t match/has no externalId), causing events to be written to the wrong calendar or fail. GoogleCalendarService was updated to select by `credentialId`, but the others were not, so the asymmetry is a real correctness issue introduced/left by the diff. The mention of CalDAV isn’t verifiable from the shown diff, but the Office365/Lark problem is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:466-478` — the legacy (no `credentialId`) branch now sits inside the per-reference loop, so with N references it issues N × M delete calls across all calendar credentials, many with mismatched uids. Hoist the legacy path outside the loop, or dedupe.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `bookingCalendarReference` changes from a single `.find(...)` to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the delete logic is changed to `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) { ... if (credentialId) { ... } else { ... } }`. That means any fallback/legacy path that deletes by iterating across all calendar credentials (because there is no `credentialId` to target a specific one) will now run once per reference, multiplying API delete attempts. Since each `reference` carries its own `uid`/`externalCalendarId`, running the fallback across *all* credentials per reference will necessarily attempt many deletions against credentials that don't own that uid/calendarId (i.e., mismatched), and with N references it becomes N×M calls. This is a behavioral regression introduced by moving to per-reference looping without deduping/hoisting the fallback logic.
